olympiad_full_name: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad
statement: Let $S(n)$ be the digit sum of $n$. Find all solutions of $n(S(n)-1)=2010$.
source: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad 2010

olympiad_full_name: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad
statement: $\triangle ABC$ with $L,M,N$ = midpoints of $BC,CA,AB$. Tangent to circumcircle at $A$ meets $LM,LN$ at $P,Q$. Show $CP\parallel BQ$.
source: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad 2010

olympiad_full_name: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad
statement: A token on an $m\times n$ board moves to adjacent squares but never revisits and no two consecutive moves in the same direction. Game ends when stuck. Find all $m,n$ for which, for some starting square, all squares are visited.
source: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad 2010

olympiad_full_name: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad
statement: Find all positive integers $N$ such that an $N\times N$ board can be tiled with $5\times 5$ or $1\times 3$ tiles (no overlaps, complete coverage).
source: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad 2010

olympiad_full_name: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad
statement: If $p,q,r$ are nonzero rationals with $\sqrt[3]{pq^2}+\sqrt[3]{qr^2}+\sqrt[3]{rp^2}$ a nonzero rational, prove $\dfrac{1}{\sqrt[3]{pq^2}}+\dfrac{1}{\sqrt[3]{qr^2}}+\dfrac{1}{\sqrt[3]{rp^2}}$ is also rational.
source: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad 2010

olympiad_full_name: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad
statement: Circles $\Gamma,\Gamma_1$ internally tangent at $A$ with radii $r>r_1$. $B$ is diametrically opposite $A$ on $\Gamma$; $C$ on $\Gamma$ with $BC$ tangent to $\Gamma_1$ at $P$. $A'$ = midpoint of $BC$. Given $O_1A'\parallel AP$, find $r/r_1$.
source: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad 2010
